selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Enhanced multicast session identity for wildcard-VLAN virtual wire pairs
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: For wildcard-VLAN VWP multicast, the session identity incorporates ingress interface and VLAN ID so identical source/group/protocol traffic in separate VLAN contexts is represented by separate multicast sessions.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Packet enters VWP member -> VLAN context is preserved -> multicast policy lookup -> session keyed with ingress interface and VLAN -> forwarding/NPU path; repeated source/group on another VLAN creates a separate session.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Cross-VLAN multicast session aliasing or VLAN-context loss; wildcard VLAN/filter/policy mismatch.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys mcast-session list shows distinct session IDs and different indev/vlanid for same source/group; policy/path counters and VLAN-aware packet capture correlate the result.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Enable wildcard-vlan on the VWP, set the intended vlan-filter, verify multicast policy ingress/egress and tagged VLAN handling, then confirm separate sessions; do not infer policy success from a single session or a capture on the wrong interface.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Same source and multicast group arriving on VLAN 50 and VLAN 60 must create separate sessions because ingress interface and VLAN are part of the VWP multicast key.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: One VWP spanning two tagged VLAN paths; same multicast source/group on both; two independent session-table rows annotated with indev and vlanid.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: No prior 30-day lesson teaches VWP multicast session-key composition; prior multicast lessons cover TTL, PIM/BSR, and shapers, not VLAN-aware session identity.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Authenticated NTPv4 time synchronization with SHA-256 keys
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager 8.0 NTP client authenticates NTPv4 server exchanges with SHA-256 using a shared key, key identifier, and explicit hex/ASCII key format.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Chrony serves NTP and loads its keyfile -> FortiManager selects server, authentication, SHA-256, key format, key and key-id -> authenticated time exchange -> diagnose system ntp status reports server state.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Time server reachable but authentication fails because key ID, algorithm, format, or secret differs; clock remains unsynchronized.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Chrony keyfile entry, FortiManager ntpserver object, and diagnose system ntp status; compare key ID and key material without exposing secrets.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Match key-id, SHA256 algorithm, hex/ASCII format and exact shared key on both sides; ensure Chrony allows the FortiManager source and keyfile is loaded; verify status and clock offset.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A reachable Chrony server rejects FortiManager NTP authentication; align the key ID and SHA-256 key format/material rather than changing routing.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager client -> routed management network -> Chrony NTP server; SHA-256 key-ID exchange shown separately from UDP reachability; status verification below.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiManager lesson covers NTP authentication or time-source integrity; prior topics cover device workflows, templates, and control-plane features.

selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer active-active geo HA allows members in separate routed data centers to receive logs from directly connected devices and forward those logs/archive files to peers and remote servers; unicast heartbeat removes the Layer-2 VIP dependency.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Two FAZ nodes configure a-a mode and peer identity -> unicast heartbeat over routed WAN -> initial sync/election -> each member ingests local device logs -> peer/remote forwarding -> FortiGate primary/alternate server failover/fallback.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Cluster stuck at initial sync, peer heartbeat blocked, VRRP filtered, or one site silently lacks log ingestion/remote forwarding.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: diagnose ha status shows role, peer, initial log sync and configuration sync; packet capture for IP protocol 112; FortiGate server/alt-server/fallback config; per-node log receipt and remote forwarding.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Disable initial-sync on at least one node during initial formation; enable unicast; permit VRRP protocol 112; omit cluster VIP across L3 sites and use heartbeat interface; configure primary/alternate FAZ and validate ingestion from devices at both sites.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Two data centers have only routed connectivity and both must ingest/forward local logs; choose active-active geo HA with unicast heartbeat and no L2 VIP.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two geographically separated data centers joined by routed WAN; each FAZ node has local FortiGate log sources; unicast heartbeat and peer log/archive forwarding; optional remote log server.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: Prior FortiAnalyzer coverage includes active-passive Fabric Supervisor HA; this lesson is a distinct active-active data-plane/log-ingestion architecture across Layer 3 sites.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: DCBX negotiation, ETS priority groups, and priority-based flow control
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitchOS 8.0 DCBX exchanges ETS configuration/recommendation, PFC configuration, and application-priority TLVs via LLDP; ETS maps CoS queues to priority groups with guaranteed bandwidth; PFC pauses selected priorities.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Ingress 802.1p CoS -> trusted Dot1p map -> egress queue -> ETS priority group -> scheduler guarantees bandwidth; LLDP DCBX advertises application priority/PFC/ETS to peer; peer negotiates compatible lossless classes.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Lossless RoCE/FCoE/iSCSI traffic drops or starves because queue mapping, DCBX TLVs, peer configuration, PFC priorities, or ETS bandwidth allocation disagree.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Supported model and FortiSwitchOS version; LLDP profile contains app-prio/ets-config/ets-rec/pfc-config; trust-dot1p-map enabled; DCBX enabled on both peers; priority-group rates total 100%; per-priority PFC settings.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Confirm eligible hardware; use Dot1p trust (not simultaneous DSCP trust on the same DCBX interface); configure DCBX on both peers; map CoS queues to PGs; separate PFC-enabled, lossy, and strict-priority groups; make ETS rates sum to 100%.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: RoCE needs lossless behavior only for its selected priority; solve by matching DCBX app-priority, queue-to-PG mapping and PFC on both peers, not global pause on all traffic.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch-to-peer Ethernet link with LLDP DCBX TLV exchange; ingress CoS map -> queues -> three ETS groups (lossy/lossless/strict) -> PFC pause on lossless priority.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: No prior 30-day FortiSwitch lesson covers DCBX, ETS, PFC, or lossless Ethernet; previous topics cover MACsec, STP, PTP, mirroring, and PoE.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Dynamic captive-portal redirect URLs from RADIUS Access-Accept
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS WiFi controller reads the Fortinet-Captive-Portal-URL RADIUS attribute (vendor attribute 27) from Access-Accept and redirects the wireless client to a session-specific portal when dynamic redirect is enabled on a tunnel-mode auth-mac captive-portal VAP.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client associates to captive-portal SSID -> MAC-auth RADIUS request -> policy engine returns Access-Accept with Fortinet-Captive-Portal-URL -> FortiGate controller applies redirect -> browser opens the returned session-specific portal.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Client lands on default/static portal or no redirect because VAP mode/type is wrong, feature disabled, or Access-Accept lacks/contains malformed attribute 27.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: VAP CLI shows captive-portal enable, portal-type auth-mac, captive-portal-dynamic-redirect-url enable; RADIUS trace shows Access-Accept and vendor attribute 27; browser redirect URL matches policy response.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Use tunnel-mode captive portal with auth-mac; enable dynamic redirect; confirm RADIUS server/group mapping and Access-Accept attribute 27 value; test authorized and unauthorized policy outcomes separately.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A session-specific portal URL is supplied in the RADIUS Access-Accept; enable dynamic redirect on a tunnel-mode auth-mac VAP and return Fortinet-Captive-Portal-URL attribute 27.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Wireless client/AP -> FortiGate WiFi controller -> RADIUS policy engine; Access-Accept carries attribute 27 back to controller; browser redirect to session-specific portal.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiAP lesson covers RADIUS-supplied dynamic portal URLs; prior portal content concerns other captive-portal controls and does not teach attribute-27 redirect selection.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: RADIUS identity normalization and LDAP domain matching for user-to-policy resolution
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC parses qualified usernames into user/domain components, applies exact configured domain matching, resolves directory identity and maps directory records to local user IDs; anonymous outer identity or a mismatched domain format can prevent LDAP group/user matching.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint sends RADIUS identity -> FortiNAC records the presented username -> parser separates user/domain -> directory selection and LDAP lookup -> local user record/user ID is matched -> user/host profile and access policy can consume identity.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Authentication succeeds at RADIUS but LDAP-backed policy does not match because the visible username is anonymous, domain format is inconsistent, or multiple directories contain duplicate IDs.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Network > RADIUS log shows username; Directory Domain Name setting; compare user, user@domain, domain\\user formats; directory synchronization and user ID record; resulting policy/user mapping.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Inspect the exact identity received; verify endpoint identity privacy behavior; make the login format and exact domain configuration consistent; remove an unintended Domain Name requirement or configure the expected UPN format; use unique LDAP identifier mappings across multiple directories.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: RADIUS log says anonymous and LDAP group policy misses; first inspect the identity sent and FortiNAC's exact domain parsing/format rules, not password validity.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Endpoint -> RADIUS identity -> FortiNAC username/domain parser -> one or more LDAP directories -> local user record -> policy/profile; anonymous identity and domain mismatch shown as branch failures.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: Prior FortiNAC lessons cover RADIUS event export, dashboards, role precedence and policy order; none covers username canonicalization, EAP identity privacy, or exact LDAP domain matching.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Local RADIUS EAP-TLS certificate revocation is OCSP-only
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F Local RADIUS validates EAP-TLS client certificate chains using RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius] and supports OCSP revocation checks; the Local RADIUS path has no CRL/CDP lookup/import option.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client presents certificate in EAP-TLS -> FortiNAC validates chain against RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius] -> reads OCSP URL from certificate AIA -> queries responder -> accepts/rejects according to status; HA control node must reach responder and have trust chain.
selected_candidates.failure_class: CDP-only certificate fails when OCSP is enabled; root/intermediate missing; OCSP URL absent/unreachable; failover node lacks applicable trust chain.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: openssl x509 output for Authority Information Access and CRL Distribution Points; Local Service OCSP setting; RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius] target; RADIUS logs and good/revoked test certificates.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Publish OCSP and include AIA OCSP URL in reissued certificates; upload all issuing roots/intermediates to RADIUS Endpoint Trust [radius] for both HA nodes; verify DNS/HTTP reachability; if CRL is mandatory, terminate EAP-TLS on an external CRL-capable RADIUS server and proxy from FortiNAC-F.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A client certificate contains CDP but no OCSP URL; Local RADIUS cannot use CDP/CRL, so issue an OCSP-enabled certificate or use an external CRL-capable RADIUS server.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: EAP-TLS endpoint certificate -> FortiNAC-F Local RADIUS -> trusted CA chain + AIA OCSP URL -> OCSP responder; separate unsupported CDP/CRL path marked unavailable; HA peer reachability.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiNAC-F lesson covers local RADIUS certificate revocation. FortiAuthenticator CRL handling is a different product workflow and is not reused.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: TACACS+ client groups as reusable policy targets and REST-managed objects
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0.2 adds TACACS+ client group objects; policies can select individual clients and/or groups; REST API exposes client-group and group-client association resources.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Network device source IP matches TACACS+ client object -> membership/group association is evaluated -> policy targeting client or group applies -> configured identity source authenticates operator -> TACACS+ response/authorization returned.
selected_candidates.failure_class: New network device is not matched by any policy because it is absent from the group or group is not selected in the policy; duplicated individual and group policy targets can create unexpected policy coverage.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Authentication > TACACS+ Service > Clients > Group membership; policy Chosen TACACS+ Client Groups; REST resources /tacplusclientgroups/ and /tacplusgroupclient/; TACACS request source IP.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Create or import client group, add the exact device client objects, attach group to intended TACACS+ policy, verify source address/NAT, and test authentication/authorization from a member device.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Hundreds of routers need one TACACS policy without selecting each one individually; create a TACACS+ client group and bind that group to the policy.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Many routers/switches -> TACACS+ client objects -> reusable client group -> policy -> identity source -> TACACS+ response; REST API shown as management plane.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiAuthenticator lesson covers TACACS+ client-group abstraction or its REST associations; prior lessons cover TACACS authorization and HA/licensing.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Reusable Guest Instruction Profiles attached to secrets
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 Guest Instruction profiles are reusable formatted guidance objects independent of secret objects; optional image/video resources use a separate instruction-resource allocation and profiles are attached to secrets.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable Guest Instruction Feature -> allocate instruction resources if media is used -> create reusable profile and resources -> attach profile in a secret's Settings -> guest checks out secret -> attached instructions render with the secret.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Guest sees no instructions because feature is disabled, profile not attached, resource allocation is zero for media, or resource reference is missing.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: System > Settings > Advanced toggle and Instruction Resources Allocation (%); Secret Settings > Instruction Profile list; resource library; secret Settings > Guest Instruction assignment; guest checkout view.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Enable feature, set resource allocation above zero when media is needed, create profile/resources, attach profile to each intended secret, and validate using a guest checkout account; replace shared resource carefully because references update.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Reusable operational guidance must appear when a guest checks out several secrets; create one instruction profile and attach it to each secret, without confusing it with access policy or credentials.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Instruction resource library -> reusable instruction profile -> multiple secret objects -> guest checkout screen; credentials/access policy shown as separate control plane.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiPAM lesson covers guest instruction profiles or resource reuse; prior PAM lessons cover gateways, RDP, backups and JIT.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Dynamic IP watchlists populated by username-to-IP lookup
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM rule action LookupIpByUser populates an IP-based watchlist from the Identity and Location database even when the triggering event has username but no IP attribute; it removes stale IP when another user takes it and updates when the user changes IP.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Rule fires with username -> Step 3 Define Action -> Watch List Edit -> LookupIpByUser -> identity/location database resolves current IP -> IP watchlist add/update/remove -> downstream rule/remediation consumes current address.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Empty or stale watchlist due missing/stale user-IP mapping, identity collection gap, or incorrect rule action configuration.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Rule action shows LookupIpByUser; Identity and Location database maps username to current IP; watchlist entry appears, changes on user IP change, and is removed on IP reassignment.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Verify identity/location data freshness and user mapping; configure LookupIpByUser in the rule's Watch List Edit action; test user address change and reassignment before enabling automatic blocking.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A rule event has username but no IP; use LookupIpByUser to resolve the current IP from Identity and Location and maintain the IP watchlist.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Username-only event -> FortiSIEM rule -> Identity & Location user-IP mapping -> LookupIpByUser -> dynamic IP watchlist -> downstream response.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiSIEM lesson covers dynamic watchlist enrichment or user-to-IP mapping; prior lessons cover investigation graphs, ML workbench and query functions.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Source IP anchoring for user/group- and country-specific egress NAT
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE source IP anchoring maps remote-user source criteria (user/group or country) at a security PoP to a dedicated public IP used for source NAT; implementation creates a policy route and firewall policy on the PoP FortiGate.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Remote user enters security PoP -> source criteria matches user/group or country -> policy route selects anchor -> firewall policy SNATs to dedicated public IP -> destination sees deterministic customer egress IP.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Wrong or shared egress IP, missing anchor/entitlement, unmatched group/country, or third-party geolocation feed has not propagated.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: IP Management > Security Public IPs > IP anchors, source criteria, PoP mapping, dedicated IP allocation/licensing, test egress IP from matched and unmatched users, public IP feed/geolocation.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Open FortiCare request for backend deployment; confirm license and additional IP allocation; map user group/country to PoP anchor; validate policy route/SNAT and external allowlist; allow third-party geolocation propagation time.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: A remote user group must always egress from a dedicated address at a PoP; use source IP anchoring and a user/group criterion, not merely geolocation metadata.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Remote user/agent -> FortiSASE PoP -> group/country match -> policy route + SNAT -> dedicated public IP -> SaaS/private destination; unanchored default path shown separately.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: No previous 30-day FortiSASE lesson covers source IP anchoring; prior topics cover DNS, tunnel readiness, IPAM control-plane subnet and DEM.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Session-affine SD-WAN load balancing using source-IP and source-destination-IP hash modes
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: SD-WAN load-balance hash-mode selects member by round-robin, source IP, source-destination IP, session weight, or measured volume; source-based hashes preserve egress-member affinity for a client or client/destination pair.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Flow matches explicit/implicit SD-WAN rule -> manual or SLA strategy selects eligible members -> hash-mode maps flow to member -> firewall session/NAT uses selected underlay -> subsequent same-key flows retain intended member affinity.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Applications that bind sessions to source IP fail when load balancing changes egress; uneven distribution is mistaken for link failure; SLA eligibility is confused with hash selection.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys sdwan service4/service6 shows mode and selected members; health-check status shows SLA eligibility; session table and egress packet capture show actual interface/NAT source; single-user policy-route test isolates algorithm effect.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Choose source-ip-based for client-level affinity or source-dest-ip-based for pair-level affinity; use SLA strategy to constrain eligible links; verify NAT and sessions; avoid round-robin/volume modes where source-IP persistence is required.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Banking site requires stable egress IP for a client/destination pair; select source-dest-ip-based (or source-ip-based if all destinations must share one path), not round-robin.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Multiple client flows -> explicit SD-WAN rule -> SLA eligibility filter -> source/destination hash -> WAN1/WAN2; stable same-key path and distinct destination path illustrated.
selected_candidates.uniqueness_assessment: Prior SD-WAN lessons cover underlay-bandwidth steering, quota steering, per-packet IPsec aggregate, SLA probe classes and ADVPN; this lesson isolates source-identity hash affinity rather than bandwidth measurement or quota logic.
